title: About
text: Valeria Ortiz-Villalobos is an Education and Psychology Ph.D. candidate at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, Michigan (expected Ph.D. defense, 2027). Her research examines language and literacy development in Spanish-English heritage bilingual children, with a focus on how cognitive skills and home and school experiences shape reading comprehension in both languages. A Rackham Predoctoral Fellow, she has published in Reading Research Quarterly and Brain and Language, and she has presented at venues including the Society for Research in Child Development and the International Symposium of Bilingualism. Before her doctoral studies, she earned an M.Sc. in Child Development and Education from the University of Oxford and worked in Costa Rica as a school psychologist, university lecturer, and early childhood education consultant.

title: About
text:
Research Experience

University of Michigan
Language & Literacy Lab (P.I. Ioulia Kovelman & Teresa Satterfield) | Graduate Research Assistant | Fall 2024 - present
Graduate Research Assistant in a multi-university, NIH-funded project on developmental language disorders in bilingual children. Developed assessment and data-collection materials, trained research assistants in administration, and led in-person data collection family sessions, including consent and parent interviews, and children’s behavioral assessment. Managed research databases and streamlined data entry, storage, and retrieval. Contributed to data analysis, publications, and oral presentations.
En Nuestra Lengua (P.I. Teresa Satterfield) | Graduate Research Assistant | Fall 2021 - present
Led school-administered child evaluations conducted routinely in fall, winter, and spring. Independently conducted data collection for a longitudinal dissertation study, including data entry, scoring, and statistical analysis. Contributed to the dissemination of findings through academic publications and presentations, as well as sharing results with participating families.


University of Oxford, United Kingdom
Families, Effective Learning and Literacy (FELL) Research Group (P.I.s Kathy Sylva, Sandra Mathers) | Graduate Research Assistant | Aug 2017 - May 2018
Co-authored with senior researchers a book chapter on a smartphone-based family intervention supporting children’s learning. Conducted literature searches across child development and education topics (e.g., preschool quality, parental support, professional development). Supported data management and SPSS data entry and trained a research intern in SPSS and statistical procedures.

title: About
text: Valeria Ortiz-Villalobos is an Education and Psychology Ph.D. candidate at the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor, Michigan (expected Ph.D. defense, 2027). Her research examines language and literacy development in Spanish-English heritage bilingual children, with a focus on how cognitive skills and home and school experiences shape reading comprehension in both languages. A Rackham Predoctoral Fellow, she has published in Reading Research Quarterly and Brain and Language, and she has presented at venues including the Society for Research in Child Development and the International Symposium of Bilingualism. Before her doctoral studies, she earned an M.Sc. in Child Development and Education from the University of Oxford and worked in Costa Rica as a school psychologist, university lecturer, and early childhood education consultant.
